```
      ┃  ██  ┃█    █┃  ██  ┃
      ┃  ██  ┃█    █┃  ██  ┃
      ┃      ┃      ┃      ┃
```

### Requirements
- Docker Engine ≥ 20.10 (or Docker Desktop)
- `bash`, and `curl` or `wget`
- *(optional)* [`fzf`](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) for the fuzzy picker

### One-liner
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RiccardoNocita/Jailed-Claude/master/install.sh | bash
```
The installer downloads the needed files from this repo into `~/.local/share/jailed-claude` and symlinks the command onto your `PATH`.

## Usage

### Basic
```bash
jailed_claude                          # pick a profile + model, then you're in Claude Code
jailed_claude -p "summarize this repo" # any Claude Code flag is passed through
```

On launch it asks, in order:
1. **Isolate from the upstream provider?** (default: *yes*)
2. **Which config profile?** (`conf/*.conf`)
3. **Which model?** (`default` = let Claude decide)

### Provider profiles

Default location:
>  $HOME/.local/share/jailed-claude/conf

Each `conf/*.conf` is a named *identity* for an LLM provider — the endpoint, credentials and models to use:

Example: **`conf/local.conf`**
```bash
JAILED_MODELS=unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF,unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434
# ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-...
# API_FORCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0
# API_TIMEOUT_MS="3600000"
```

`conf/default.conf` ships with **no** environment variables, so Claude Code runs exactly as it would natively. This is how you "manage provider identities": one file per provider, chosen at launch.

### Isolated mode (network lockdown)
By default the wrapper asks whether to isolate; press Enter (yes) and it rewrites `/etc/hosts` inside the container to point every host in the blocklist at `127.0.0.1`. Result: **no** traffic to those upstreams — only your local endpoint works. Useful for:

- **Privacy** — source code never leaves the machine
- **Integrity** — nothing remote can alter behaviour or push unwanted changes
- **No auto-updates / telemetry** — the upstream is simply unreachable

Force it from the CLI with `--isolated` (skips the prompt).

#### Custom blocklist (`JAILED_CLAUDE_BLOCK_HOSTS`)
The list of blackholed hosts defaults to the Anthropic domains and can be fully replaced via the `JAILED_CLAUDE_BLOCK_HOSTS` environment variable (space-separated hostnames):

```bash
# Block Anthropic plus any other host you want unreachable
export JAILED_CLAUDE_BLOCK_HOSTS="api.anthropic.com statsig.anthropic.com sentry.io"
jailed_claude --isolated
```

Malformed entries are skipped with a warning; if no valid host remains, the wrapper refuses to start in isolated mode (an empty list would silently disable isolation). The active list is printed on launch.

> **Limitations — read this.** The lockdown works at the *name-resolution* layer only:
> - hosts **not** in the list resolve and connect normally — this is not an air gap;
> - direct IP connections, DNS-over-HTTPS or hardcoded endpoints bypass it;
> - `host.docker.internal` is mapped by default for local gateways — you can cut it with `JAILED_ALLOW_INTERNAL=0`.
>
> For a hard guarantee, run the container on a dedicated Docker network with egress filtering (or `--network=none` plus an allow-listed proxy).

## Configuration reference

### Keys inside a `conf/*.conf` file
| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `JAILED_MODELS` | Comma-separated model IDs offered in the picker (`default` is always added) |
| any other `KEY=VALUE` | Passed to the container as an environment variable (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) |

> Values are read **verbatim to the end of the line**: there is no inline-comment support, so put `#` comments on their own line. Surrounding single/double quotes are stripped and an optional `export ` prefix is tolerated.

### Environment overrides (for automation / non-interactive use)
| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `JAILED_CLAUDE_IMAGE` | Docker image tag (default `jailed-claude:latest`) |
| `JAILED_CONF` | Skip the profile picker and use this conf file directly |
| `JAILED_CLAUDE_BLOCK_HOSTS` | Space-separated hostnames to blackhole in isolated mode (default: Anthropic domains — see *Custom blocklist*) |
| `JAILED_ALLOW_INTERNAL` | Map `host.docker.internal` to the host gateway. Default: enabled; set `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` to drop the mapping (gateway profiles that use that hostname will then fail) |

## Project layout
```
jailed-claude/
├── jailed-claude              # wrapper / entrypoint
├── Dockerfile.jailed-claude   # sandbox image definition
├── install.sh                 # remote installer (curl | bash)
├── conf/
│   ├── default.conf           # stock Claude Code (no env vars)
│   └── local.conf             # example local-gateway profile
└── docs/                      # screenshots referenced in the README
```

## Security notes
- The container only ever sees your CWD + `~/.claude{,.json}`; the rest of your filesystem is invisible to it.
- All Linux capabilities are dropped and privilege escalation is disabled.
- In isolated mode, egress to the listed upstreams is cut at the name-resolution layer (see *Limitations* in the Isolated mode section).
- For a stricter sandbox you can add `--read-only --tmpfs /tmp` to the run (see source).

## Uninstall
```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/jailed_claude            # or wherever the symlink lives
rm -rf ~/.local/share/jailed-claude
docker rmi jailed-claude:latest             # optional
```

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# AI/ML Questions

**English** · [Español](README.es.md)

Free multiple-choice questions for learning artificial intelligence and machine learning, from the basics to research topics. Every option explains why it is right or wrong, and every question cites its sources.

**Try it: https://ai-ml-questions.strangemachines.workers.dev/**

- **103 questions in English and Spanish**, in 8 topics and three levels. Study mode shows the explanation after each answer; exam mode, the results at the end.
- **The answer does not show in the wording.** The questions follow Haladyna's item-writing rules, and a validator checks them: for example, it warns when the correct option is noticeably longer than the others.
- **Measured with real answers.** Answers are recorded anonymously, with no cookies; once a question has enough of them, they show its real difficulty and which distractors nobody falls for ([details](docs/statistics.md)).
- **Open questions.** They are JSON files with a schema, under CC BY-SA 4.0, so you can reuse them in a course, in flashcards or in your own app.
- **No account.** Once loaded it works offline, and it can be installed on a phone.

**Alpha version.** The questions are drafts that a person has not reviewed yet. If you find a mistake, use the "Report a mistake" link under the question or [open an issue](https://github.com/CristobalSantana/ai-ml-questions/issues).

## Topics

| Topic | For example |
|---|---|
| Classical machine learning | Bias and variance, gradient boosting, Gaussian processes, dataset shift, Q-learning |
| Neural networks | Backpropagation, optimizers, LSTMs, mixture of experts, PINNs, KANs |
| Transformers & LLMs | Attention, the context window and KV cache, prompting, LoRA, RLHF |
| Retrieval & RAG | BM25, embeddings, HNSW, chunking, reranking, RAG evaluation |
| Computer vision | Convolution, detection, segmentation, ViT, CLIP |
| Agents, harness & phenomena | Tool use, MCP, prompt injection, double descent, grokking, sycophancy |
| Evaluation & responsible AI | Precision and recall, calibration, LLM-as-judge, fairness, privacy |
| Landmark papers | From the perceptron (1958) to FlashAttention (2022) |

## How the questions are made

Each question states its level in Bloom's taxonomy and gets an estimated difficulty from a rubric. A validator checks the format and the writing rules, and a second model checks facts, sources and the translation before a person approves the question. Once a question has enough answers, they also show whether it tells apart people who know more. The details are in [`docs/`](docs/README.md).

## Contributing

The most useful help right now is checking questions, because a person has not reviewed them all yet:

- **Report a mistake** with the link under each question, or [open an issue](https://github.com/CristobalSantana/ai-ml-questions/issues).
- **Review the questions of an area you know:** the key, the explanations and the sources.
- **Improve the Spanish**, or **propose new questions**.

[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) explains how. Issues and pull requests can be written in English or Spanish.

## Run it locally

```bash
pip install jsonschema
python scripts/validate.py                    # checks the questions
python scripts/build_site.py --include-drafts # builds site/data
python -m http.server 8000 --directory site   # then open http://localhost:8000
```

## Repository

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `questions/` | The questions, one JSON file per area |
| `taxonomy.json` | Topics, areas and subtopics, in English and Spanish |
| `schema/` | The format of a question |
| `scripts/` | The validator, the site builder and the statistics of each question |
| `prompts/` | Prompts for generating and reviewing questions, in English and in their original Spanish |
| `site/` | The website |
| `worker/`, `migrations/` | The Cloudflare Worker that stores the anonymous answers, and their table |
| `docs/` | The full documentation |

## License

The questions are under [CC BY-SA 4.0](LICENSE-QUESTIONS): you can reuse them if you credit the source and share under the same license. The code is under [MIT](LICENSE), and the fonts under the SIL Open Font License.

If the site helps you, a star on GitHub helps more people find it. You can also support it on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/strangemachines).

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
Your Spark code. No JVM. One engine for batch, streaming and always-fresh views.

**Krishiv** is a Rust-native, Spark-compatible compute engine we are building for the agentic era. Keep the PySpark
and Spark SQL you already write, and run it on a vectorized, Arrow-native engine that handles **batch SQL**,
**streaming** and **incrementally maintained materialized views** with the same semantics. Start in-process on a
laptop, and take the same code to a single server or a cluster.

> [!WARNING]
> **Pre-alpha: under active construction, not usable yet.** There is no working query engine, no release and no
> stable API. Everything below describes what we are building, not what exists today.

   ⭐ Star the repo and 👀 Watch → Custom → Releases to follow development from the first commit to 1.0.

## Why Krishiv

| | Design goal | What it means for you |
|---|---|---|
| 🦀 | **Spark-compatible, no JVM** | Keep your PySpark and Spark SQL code. Spark Connect clients connect directly; execution is Rust-native and vectorized. |
| 🔁 | **One engine: batch, streaming, incremental** | The same SQL and the same semantics everywhere. A batch query is just a bounded stream. |
| 📦 | **Embedded → single-node → distributed** | `pip install krishiv` or `cargo add krishiv` to start in-process, then scale out without rewriting your code. |
| ⚡ | **Always-fresh materialized views** | Views update incrementally as data changes (DBSP-inspired incremental computation), and streaming state is directly queryable. |
| 🤖 | **Built for the agentic era** | A built-in MCP server lets AI agents explore and query your data; Arrow-native, zero-copy interop with pandas, Polars and PyArrow. |
| ✅ | **Open and correctness-first** | Apache-2.0. Tested against real Spark behaviour with golden fixtures and differential testing. |

## How it fits

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph APIs["Your code"]
        A1["PySpark via Spark Connect"]
        A2["SQL"]
        A3["Python DataFrames"]
        A4["Rust"]
        A5["MCP for AI agents"]
        A6["Arrow Flight SQL"]
    end
    subgraph Engine["One Krishiv engine"]
        E1["Batch"]
        E2["Streaming"]
        E3["Incremental views"]
    end
    subgraph Deploy["Run it anywhere"]
        D1["Embedded"]
        D2["Single-node"]
        D3["Distributed"]
    end
    subgraph Lake["Your lakehouse"]
        L1["Parquet"]
        L2["Apache Iceberg"]
        L3["Delta Lake"]
    end
    APIs --> Engine --> Deploy --> Lake
```

## Status and roadmap at a glance

Krishiv is in **pre-alpha**. The workspace layout, CI quality gates, Spark error-class and config registries, a test
kit with Spark golden fixtures, and the Python package skeleton are in place. The query engine itself is being built
now.

| Milestone | Focus | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Embedded core alpha | In-process SQL and DataFrames on Arrow, with Python and Rust APIs | 🚧 In progress |
| 2. Spark Connect and lakehouse | PySpark over Spark Connect; Parquet, Iceberg and Delta | ⏳ Planned |
| 3. Streaming | Stateful streaming with the same SQL and semantics as batch | ⏳ Planned |
| 4. Incremental views | Always-fresh materialized views and queryable state | ⏳ Planned |
| 5. Distributed | Scale out to a cluster with the same code | ⏳ Planned |
| 6. 1.0 | Stable APIs and formats | ⏳ Planned |

Watch **Releases** to hear when the first alpha lands.

## What it will look like

> [!NOTE]
> **Planned API (not yet available).** These snippets show the intended experience and may change.

**Python: your existing PySpark code, pointed at Krishiv over Spark Connect.**

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F

# Planned: a local Krishiv server speaking the Spark Connect protocol.
spark = SparkSession.builder.remote("sc://localhost:15002").getOrCreate()

orders = spark.read.parquet("s3://lake/orders/")
daily = orders.groupBy("order_date").agg(F.sum("amount").alias("revenue"))

daily.toPandas()  # results arrive as Arrow
```

**Python: the native Krishiv API — same code, embedded in your process.**

```python
import krishiv
from krishiv.sql import functions as F

# Planned: PySpark-compatible API running in-process — no server, no JVM.
spark = krishiv.SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()

orders = spark.read.parquet("s3://lake/orders/")
daily = orders.groupBy("order_date").agg(F.sum("amount").alias("revenue"))

daily.to_arrow()   # zero-copy Arrow table (also .to_polars(), .toPandas())
# Same code against a cluster: krishiv.SparkSession.builder.remote("sc://...")
```

**SQL: an always-fresh view over a stream.**

```sql
-- Planned syntax.
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW revenue_by_region AS
SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM orders_stream
GROUP BY region;

-- Reads the latest result, maintained incrementally as events arrive.
SELECT * FROM revenue_by_region ORDER BY revenue DESC;
```

## Follow along and get involved

- ⭐ **Star** the repo and 👀 **Watch → Releases** to get notified about alphas and milestones.
- 🐛 Report bugs or share ideas in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/KrishivAI/krishiv-engine/issues).
- 🛠️ Read the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build, test, DCO sign-off and PR rules.
- 🤝 Please follow our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- 🔒 Report security issues privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- 🌐 Learn more at [krishiv.ai](https://krishiv.ai).

Some code comments reference design records (for example "ADR 0034") that are kept private for now; see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for what this means for contributors.

# lakehouse-quality-gates

**Soda data contracts for bronze, silver and gold, with audited snapshot publication.**

[CI](https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/lakehouse-quality-gates/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[Release](https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/lakehouse-quality-gates/releases/tag/v1.0.0)
[Python 3.12](https://www.python.org/)
[License: MIT](LICENSE)
[Coverage 97%](docs/results/README.md)
[Soda Core 4.26](https://docs.soda.io/)
[Article on Medium](https://medium.com/data-engineer-things/data-quality-before-publication-building-gates-for-a-lakehouse-4d57dabd8fa7)

## What it does

Each layer of the [local-data-lakehouse](https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/local-data-lakehouse) medallion gets a
declarative [Soda Core v4](https://docs.soda.io/) contract (53 checks in total). A gate verifies the contract right after
the layer is built, on DuckDB or Trino over Apache Iceberg. If it fails, the Airflow task fails and nothing downstream
is built from bad data. With **write-audit-publish**, each layer is first written to an Iceberg audit branch and only
fast-forwarded to `main` when its gate passes. Publication uses the exact audited snapshots; each table
advances separately. Quality guarantees cover the checks declared in the contracts.

## Quick start

1. **Check the prerequisites:** [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Git and Make. Docker is only needed for the live steps.

   ```bash
   uv --version && git --version && make --version | head -1
   ```

   Expected: three version lines (uv 0.5 or newer). uv installs Python 3.12 itself if it is missing.

2. **Clone the repository.**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/lakehouse-quality-gates.git && cd lakehouse-quality-gates
   ```

   Expected: a `lakehouse-quality-gates` folder, now your working directory.

3. **Create your `.env`.**

   ```bash
   make env
   ```

   Expected: `.env ready`. The defaults work for the local demo; every setting is documented in `.env.example`.

4. **Install.**

   ```bash
   make venv
   ```

   Expected: a `.venv` with Python 3.12, Soda Core 4.26, DuckDB and the dev tools, built from `uv.lock`.

5. **Validate the contracts.**

   ```bash
   make validate
   ```

   Expected: `ok` for each of the five contracts, exit code 0.

6. **Run the good batch.**

   ```bash
   make demo-good
   ```

   Expected: `retail/bronze`, `retail/silver` and `retail/gold` each report `passed` (53 checks in total).

7. **Run the bad batch.**

   ```bash
   make demo-bad
   ```

   Expected: `OK: bronze blocked as expected`, then the same for silver and gold. The reasons are in `reports/*.md`.

## Run against the live lakehouse

1. **Clone [local-data-lakehouse](https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/local-data-lakehouse) next to this repository.**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/santoshshinde2012/local-data-lakehouse.git ../local-data-lakehouse
   ```

   Expected: `../local-data-lakehouse` exists. Docker must be running, with at least 2 GB for this step.

2. **Point `.env` at it.**

   ```bash
   echo "DQ_LDL_REPO_PATH=../local-data-lakehouse" >> .env
   ```

   Expected: no output; `scripts/e2e.sh` and the live tests read this path.

3. **Run the live end-to-end check.**

   ```bash
   make e2e-live
   ```

   Expected: a summary table ending in `RESULT: PASS` (9 steps, about a minute). The good batch passes on the live
   Iceberg tables, the bad batch is blocked at every layer, and the stack is stopped again with its volumes kept.

## Full stack (Trino, Docker, Airflow)

1. **Run the full end-to-end check** (give Docker 8 GB).

   ```bash
   make e2e-full                      # or: AIRFLOW_API_PORT=8090 make e2e-full, if port 8080 is taken
   ```

   Expected: `RESULT: PASS` after 15 steps (17 to 30 minutes): the Spark pipeline, Trino gates, the `ldl-soda`
   runner container, an Airflow run that succeeds and one that stops at `dq_bronze`.

## Write-audit-publish

1. **Start the lakehouse with the WAP overlay**, then publish a good batch through audit branches.

   ```bash
   make wap-up
   make wap-demo-good
   ```

   Expected: bronze, silver and gold each `passed`, and one line per table such as
   `published bronze.orders_raw: main 6960… -> 6313… (22 rows)`.

2. **Send the bad batch.**

   ```bash
   make wap-demo-bad
   ```

   Expected: `retail/bronze: blocked`, `main stays  `, the audit branch kept with the bad rows, and
   `OK: blocked as expected, main untouched`.

3. **Run it all with Airflow and the WAP tests.**

   ```bash
   make e2e-wap                       # or: AIRFLOW_API_PORT=8090 make e2e-wap
   ```

   Expected: `RESULT: PASS` after 11 steps (about 12 minutes), including an Airflow run where `dq_bronze` fails and
   `publish_bronze` never runs.

How it works: [write-audit-publish](docs/architecture/write-audit-publish.md) · proof with snapshot ids:
[WAP run](docs/results/runs/2026-10-14-wap/README.md).

## Testing

| Command | Tier | Needs | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `make test-all` | Lint, mypy, unit + integration tests, contract validation, demo | Python | about 20 s |
